svg.title: A made-up illustration of predicting towards the centre
svg.desc: Scatter plot of 240 made-up households. Actual spending is along the bottom and the model's prediction up the side. The predictions are bunched closer together than the actual figures. Most of the poorest tenth, in orange, sit above the dashed line, which means they are predicted to spend more than they do.
svg.text: Why a model like this pulls towards the centre
Made-up data, drawn to illustrate the idea. These are not SHA or Lighthouse figures.
Actual spending (made-up scale, low to high)
Above the line: predicted to spend more than they do
Below the line: predicted to spend less
